Module 117 — Comics: Character Consistency & Lettering: English: How To Draw Your Character Consistently Patricia Caldeira (Don Corgi) A free, practical guide to turnarounds, expression sheets and practice habits for keeping a character on model. Recommends keeping a character consistent with a turnaround (usually four views, or eight for animation) that records every design detail and a color palette, a large expression sheet, and lots of practice drawing the character, keeping the design simple enough to draw often while accepting that it can evolve over time.

Module 117 — Comics: Character Consistency & Lettering: English: You can now keep characters on model and letter a page cleanly. Module 118 moves from Western comics to manga, with its own reading direction, screentones and storytelling conventions. | Hinglish: Ab tum characters ko on model rakh sakte/sakti ho aur page ko clean tareeke se letter kar sakte/sakti ho. Module 112 Western comics se manga ki taraf badhta hai, jahan reading direction, screentones aur storytelling conventions apne alag hote hain.

Module 118 — Manga Fundamentals: English: Open a manga from what looks like the back and every habit from Western comics flips: the eye enters at the top right, and the whole page is built to carry it left. | Hinglish: Manga ko us taraf se kholiye jo Western comics mein back lagti hai, aur aapki har aadat ulat jaati hai: nazar top right se shuru hoti hai, aur poora page use left ki taraf le jaane ke liye banaya jaata hai.

Module 118 — Manga Fundamentals: English: Modules 116 and 123 taught page flow, consistent characters and lettering. Manga uses the same foundations but with its own reading direction, its own workflow and its own visual shorthand, so knowing those conventions is what separates a Western comic drawn in a manga style from real manga. | Hinglish: Modules 110 aur 123 mein aapne page flow, consistent characters aur lettering seekhi. Manga mein bhi yehi buniyadi cheezein hoti hain, lekin uski apni reading direction, workflow aur visual shorthand hoti hai. In conventions ko jaanna hi Western comic ko manga style mein draw karne aur asli manga banane ke beech ka farq hai.

Module 118 — Manga Fundamentals: English: It is also one of the most structured production workflows in this arc. Script, storyboard, pencils, inks, tones and final touches each have a clear job, and learning them in order is the quickest way to finish a first short story instead of abandoning it. | Hinglish: Is arc mein manga production ke sabse structured workflows mein se ek hai. Script, storyboard, pencils, inks, tones aur final touches—har step ka apna clear kaam hai. Inhe sahi order mein seekhna pehli short story poori karne ka sabse tez tareeka hai, bajaye use beech mein chhod dene ke.

Module 118 — Manga Fundamentals: English: Traditional manga reads from right to left. The first panel sits at the upper right of the right-hand page and each row moves leftward, so pages are composed for that path and every layout decision, from panel order to balloon placement, has to respect it. | Hinglish: Traditional manga right to left padhi jaati hai. Pehla panel right-hand page ke upper right mein hota hai aur har row left ki taraf badhti hai. Isliye pages isi raaste ke liye compose kiye jaate hain, aur panel order se lekar balloon placement tak har layout decision ko iska dhyaan rakhna hota hai.

Module 118 — Manga Fundamentals: English: The workflow runs in a fixed order: scripting (theme, characters and sequences that each hold together by place, time or action), a storyboard that plans panel composition, a pencil sketch, inking, filling in details and blacks, and final touches. Skipping the storyboard stage is how pages end up redrawn. | Hinglish: Workflow ek fixed order mein chalta hai: scripting (theme, characters aur aise sequences jo place, time ya action ke hisaab se ek saath judte hain), panel composition plan karne wala storyboard, pencil sketch, inking, details aur blacks bharna, aur final touches. Storyboard stage chhodne par pages ko dobara draw karna padta hai.

Module 118 — Manga Fundamentals: English: Variety keeps pages alive. Vary the size of the boxes and the distance of the shots (close-ups, medium shots and full shots) to avoid monotony, and remember that when a manga is opened the eye tends to land at the top of the left-hand page, which makes it a strong place for a significant drawing or a reveal. | Hinglish: Variety se pages engaging rehte hain. Monotony se bachne ke liye boxes ke size aur shots ki distance (close-ups, medium shots aur full shots) mein variation rakhein. Yaad rakhein ki manga kholne par nazar aksar left-hand page ke top par jaati hai, isliye koi important drawing ya reveal rakhne ke liye yeh ek strong jagah hai.

Module 118 — Manga Fundamentals: English: Manga has its own visual shorthand. Speed lines and flashes express motion and impact, and screentones (patterned overlays used for shading and backgrounds) give pages their characteristic texture. Clean the page before adding tone, and use white to correct and add highlights at the end. | Hinglish: Manga ki apni visual shorthand hoti hai. Speed lines aur flashes movement aur impact dikhate hain, aur screentones (shading aur backgrounds ke liye use hone wale patterned overlays) pages ko unki khaas texture dete hain. Tone add karne se pehle page saaf karein, aur aakhir mein correction aur highlights ke liye white use karein.

Module 118 — Manga Fundamentals: English: Starting finished pencils or inks before a storyboard has settled the composition of the page. | Hinglish: Page ki composition storyboard mein final hone se pehle finished pencils ya inks shuru kar dena.

Module 118 — Manga Fundamentals: English: Using panels of the same size and the same shot distance throughout, which flattens the pacing. | Hinglish: Har jagah ek hi size ke panels aur ek hi shot distance use karna, jisse pacing flat ho jaati hai.

Module 118 — Manga Fundamentals: English: Laying out pages in left-to-right order and forgetting that readers will move right to left. | Hinglish: Pages ko left-to-right order mein lay out karna aur yeh bhool jaana ki readers right to left padhenge.

Module 118 — Manga Fundamentals: English: Adding screentone to a dirty or unfinished page instead of cleaning the surface first. | Hinglish: Surface saaf kiye bina dirty ya unfinished page par screentone lagana.

Module 118 — Manga Fundamentals: English: Placing the biggest moment of a spread somewhere the eye does not naturally land, instead of using the top of the left-hand page. | Hinglish: Spread ke sabse bade moment ko aisi jagah rakhna jahan nazar naturally nahi jaati, bajaye left-hand page ke top ko use karne ke.

Module 118 — Manga Fundamentals: English: Storyboard each sequence the way a film director would, thinking about how many panels you need and how to balance the page before you draw anything finished. | Hinglish: Har sequence ka storyboard film director ki tarah banayein. Kuch bhi finished draw karne se pehle sochein ki kitne panels chahiye aur page ka balance kaise rakhna hai.

Module 118 — Manga Fundamentals: English: Mix shot distances on purpose: a close-up for emotion, a medium shot for action, a full shot to establish the scene. | Hinglish: Shot distances soch-samajhkar mix karein: emotion ke liye close-up, action ke liye medium shot, aur scene establish karne ke liye full shot.

Module 118 — Manga Fundamentals: English: Ink the panel borders first, then the dialogue balloons, then the characters and settings, and add speed lines and other effects last. | Hinglish: Sabse pehle panel borders ink karein, phir dialogue balloons, uske baad characters aur settings; speed lines aur doosre effects sabse aakhir mein add karein.

Module 118 — Manga Fundamentals: English: Keep a light layer or light-colored pencil for roughs and panel borders so it does not compete with the final line art. | Hinglish: Roughs aur panel borders ke liye halki layer ya light-colored pencil use karein, taaki woh final line art ke saath compete na kare.
Module 118 — Manga Fundamentals: English: I can read and compose a page in right-to-left order. | Hinglish: Main page ko right-to-left order mein padh aur compose kar sakta/sakti hoon.

Module 118 — Manga Fundamentals: English: I can move through script, storyboard, pencils, inks, fills and final touches in order. | Hinglish: Main script, storyboard, pencils, inks, fills aur final touches ko sahi order mein kar sakta/sakti hoon.

Module 118 — Manga Fundamentals: English: I can vary panel sizes and shot distances to control pacing. | Hinglish: Main pacing control karne ke liye panel sizes aur shot distances mein variation la sakta/sakti hoon.

Module 118 — Manga Fundamentals: English: I can use speed lines, screentone and white correction as part of the finish. | Hinglish: Main finish ke hissa ke taur par speed lines, screentone aur white correction use kar sakta/sakti hoon.

Module 118 — Manga Fundamentals: English: Take a manga page you admire and number the panels in the order you read them, right to left and top to bottom, then note how the layout supports that path. | Hinglish: Apni pasand ka ek manga page lein aur panels ko padhne ke order mein number karein—right to left aur top to bottom. Phir note karein ki layout is reading path ko kaise support karta hai.

Module 118 — Manga Fundamentals: English: Storyboard a two-page scene with page one on the right and page two on the left, varying panel sizes and shot distances. | Hinglish: Ek two-page scene ka storyboard banayein, jisme page one right par aur page two left par ho. Panel sizes aur shot distances mein variation rakhein.

Module 118 — Manga Fundamentals: English: Take one storyboarded page through pencils, inks and tone, ordering the steps as the Canson workflow does. | Hinglish: Ek storyboarded page ko pencils, inks aur tone ke stages se guzarein, aur steps ko Canson workflow ke order mein karein.

Module 118 — Manga Fundamentals: English: Design a two-page spread where a major reveal lands at the top of the left-hand page, and test it on a reader to see if their eye goes there. | Hinglish: Ek two-page spread design karein jisme ek bada reveal left-hand page ke top par aaye. Phir kisi reader par test karein ki uski nazar wahan jaati hai ya nahi.

Module 118 — Manga Fundamentals: English: In what order does traditional manga read? Left to right, top to bottom Right to left, with the first panel at the upper right of the right-hand page Bottom to top Whichever order the panels are numbered Traditional manga reads right to left, so the first box is at the upper right of the right-hand page. | Hinglish: Traditional manga kis order mein padhi jaati hai? Left to right, top to bottom Right to left, jisme pehla panel right-hand page ke upper right mein hota hai Bottom to top Panels ko jis order mein number kiya gaya ho Traditional manga right to left padhi jaati hai, isliye pehla box right-hand page ke upper right mein hota hai.

Module 118 — Manga Fundamentals: English: Why vary the size of boxes and the type of shot on a manga page? To fit more panels Because it is required by publishers To make the drawings easier To avoid monotony and keep the page and pacing interesting Mixing sizes and shot distances (close-ups, medium and full shots) keeps pages from feeling repetitive. | Hinglish: Manga page par boxes ke size aur shots ke type mein variation kyun rakhni chahiye? Taaki zyada panels fit ho sakein Kyunki publishers ka yeh rule hai Taaki drawings banana aasaan ho Monotony se bachne aur page aur pacing ko interesting banaye rakhne ke liye Alag sizes aur shot distances (close-ups, medium aur full shots) mix karne se pages repetitive nahi lagte.

Module 118 — Manga Fundamentals: English: Where does the eye tend to land when a manga is opened, according to the Canson guide? The top of the left-hand page, which makes it a good spot for something significant The bottom of the right-hand page The exact center of the spread The page number The guide suggests placing a particularly significant drawing or action at the top of the left-hand page because the eye naturally goes there. | Hinglish: Canson guide ke mutabik, manga kholne par nazar aksar kahan jaati hai? Left-hand page ke top par, jo kisi important cheez ke liye achhi jagah hai Right-hand page ke bottom par Spread ke bilkul center mein Page number par Guide kehti hai ki khaas taur par important drawing ya action left-hand page ke top par rakhein, kyunki nazar naturally wahan jaati hai.

Module 118 — Manga Fundamentals: English: What should you do before adding screens (screentone) to the original drawing? Add the dialogue first Erase all the inks Clean the surface of the original drawing Skip inking The workflow advises cleaning the surface of your original drawing before adding a screen so the tone applies cleanly. | Hinglish: Original drawing par screens (screentone) add karne se pehle kya karna chahiye? Pehle dialogue add karein Saari inks mita dein Original drawing ki surface saaf karein Inking chhod dein Workflow ke mutabik, screen add karne se pehle original drawing ki surface saaf karein, taaki tone saaf-suthre tareeke se lage.

Module 118 — Manga Fundamentals: English: What is the storyboard stage for? Choosing fonts for the balloons Planning panel composition, how many boxes you need and how to balance the page before finished drawing Coloring the final pages Printing the volume The storyboard works like a film director's sketch of the panels, settling composition and balance before pencils and inks. | Hinglish: Storyboard stage kis kaam aata hai? Balloons ke liye fonts chunne ke liye Finished drawing se pehle panel composition, zaroori boxes ki ginti aur page ka balance plan karne ke liye Final pages ko color karne ke liye Volume print karne ke liye Storyboard film director ke panels wale sketch ki tarah kaam karta hai; pencils aur inks se pehle composition aur balance tay karta hai.

Module 118 — Manga Fundamentals: English: How to draft and panel MANGA PAGES | DrawlikeaSir Draw like a Sir A free 9-minute tutorial from a working manga artist on drawing panels so that the page flows well while reading. A tutorial about how to draw the panels on a manga page so that they flow better while reading, with sections on storyboarding your manga, the most common paneling mistake, reading flow, drawing focus points and using speech bubbles.

Module 118 — Manga Fundamentals: English: 6 Manga Paneling Rules for Beginner Mangaka Learn to Draw Manga A free 12-minute video of paneling rules for beginner manga artists. Paneling rules for beginner manga artists. Chapters: Rule #1; Rule #2; Rule #3; Rule #4; Rule #5; BONUS TIP.

Module 118 — Manga Fundamentals: English: Make your OWN MANGA | Tutorial on how to Storyboard | DrawlikeaSir Draw like a Sir A free 12-minute walkthrough of planning a manga from story to storyboard. Explains how manga paneling works, how to plan out your manga story, and how to create a storyboard for it.

Module 118 — Manga Fundamentals: English: Clean Manga Pages with Screentones | Beginner Guide Learn to Draw Manga A free 10-minute beginner guide to screentones, the patterned shading that gives manga pages their look. A beginner guide to using screentones to clean up and finish manga pages. Chapters: What Even Are Screentones?; Digital Screentones 101; How Do Mangakas Actually Use Screentones?; Don't Overdo It!.

Module 118 — Manga Fundamentals: English: 6 steps to drawing your manga Canson A free step-by-step manga workflow from script to final touches, including reading direction and panel variety. Walks through six steps: scripting (theme, characters and sequences with unity of place, time or action), a storyboard that plans panel composition and varies box sizes and shots, a pencil sketch, inking panel borders then characters and effects like speed lines, filling in details, blacks and screens, and final touches such as white for corrections and highlights. It also notes that traditional manga reads right to left, so the first box sits at the upper right of the right-hand page.

Module 118 — Manga Fundamentals: English: You now know manga's reading direction, workflow and visual shorthand. Module 119 moves to webtoons, where the page becomes a vertical scroll and the layout rules change again. | Hinglish: Ab aap manga ki reading direction, workflow aur visual shorthand jaante hain. Module 113 mein webtoons par baat hogi, jahan page ek vertical scroll ban jaata hai aur layout ke rules phir se badal jaate hain.

Module 119 — Webtoon & Vertical Scroll Storytelling: English: A webtoon reader sees one panel at a time, so the space between panels is not empty. It is the timing of your story. | Hinglish: Webtoon reader ek waqt mein sirf ek panel dekhta hai, isliye panels ke beech ki jagah khaali nahi hoti. Wahi aapki story ki timing hoti hai.

Module 119 — Webtoon & Vertical Scroll Storytelling: English: Modules 116 to 124 built page-based thinking: panels arranged on a page, read in a Z or right-to-left path. A webtoon removes the page entirely. The reader scrolls, and everything you learned about pacing has to be rebuilt around a single column on a phone. | Hinglish: Modules 110 se 124 tak page-based soch par focus tha: page par arranged panels, jinhe Z ya right-to-left path mein padha jaata hai. Webtoon mein page hota hi nahi. Reader scroll karta hai, aur pacing ke baare mein jo kuch aapne seekha hai, use phone ki ek single column ke hisaab se dobara plan karna padta hai.

Module 119 — Webtoon & Vertical Scroll Storytelling: English: Webtoons are also a major professional route for new comic artists, because the format is built for mobile reading and episodic release. Learning the format's own rules, instead of cropping a page layout into a strip, is what makes the work feel native. | Hinglish: Webtoons naye comic artists ke liye ek bada professional raasta bhi hain, kyunki yeh format mobile reading aur episodic release ke liye bana hai. Page layout ko bas crop karke strip bana dene ke bajay, format ke apne rules seekhne se artwork native feel karta hai.

Module 119 — Webtoon & Vertical Scroll Storytelling: English: A webtoon is a vertical comic that gives readers a cinematic impression, because they see only one panel at a time instead of many on a page. The creator controls the pacing of the story through where panels are placed, and because most readers use mobile devices, the layout should be comfortable on a phone. | Hinglish: Webtoon ek vertical comic hota hai jo readers ko cinematic impression deta hai, kyunki page par ek saath kai panels dekhne ke bajay unhe ek waqt mein sirf ek panel nazar aata hai. Creator panels kahan place karta hai, usse story ki pacing control hoti hai. Aur kyunki zyadaatar readers mobile devices use karte hain, layout phone par dekhne mein comfortable hona chahiye.

Module 119 — Webtoon & Vertical Scroll Storytelling: English: One creator's rules of thumb for panels: show at most two panels on the screen at a time, keep to about three dialogues per panel, vary panel width, shape and size to emphasize important scenes, leave at least about 250 px between panels and roughly 1000 px to signal a change in time, and make text large enough to read with motion and sound effects where they help. | Hinglish: Panels ke liye ek creator ke kuch rules of thumb: screen par ek waqt mein zyada se zyada do panels dikhayein, har panel mein lagbhag teen dialogues rakhein, important scenes ko emphasize karne ke liye panel ki width, shape aur size vary karein, panels ke beech kam se kam lagbhag 250 px aur time change dikhane ke liye kareeb 1000 px ki jagah chhodein, aur text itna bada rakhein ki aasani se padha ja sake. Jahan madad mile, wahan motion aur sound effects bhi use karein.

Module 119 — Webtoon & Vertical Scroll Storytelling: English: A webtoon storyboard plans four things: panel layout (shape and size, top-to-bottom order, whitespace as a dramatic pause), character position and composition (rough stick figures, close-up, medium or long shot, and who dominates the panel), expressions and gestures that carry emotion, and dialogue with a clear reading order that avoids overcrowded bubbles. | Hinglish: Webtoon storyboard mein chaar cheezon ki planning hoti hai: panel layout (shape aur size, upar se neeche ka order, aur dramatic pause ki tarah whitespace), character position aur composition (rough stick figures, close-up, medium ya long shot, aur panel mein kis character ka zyada dominance hai), emotion dikhane wale expressions aur gestures, aur clear reading order ke saath dialogue, jisme speech bubbles bahut crowded na hon.

Module 119 — Webtoon & Vertical Scroll Storytelling: English: Panel types each have a job: standard rectangles for stable, easy reading, tall vertical panels for towering things, falling or slowing the pace, wide panels for landscapes and calm, close-ups for emotion, establishing shots for context, splash panels for climaxes, inset panels for small details, borderless panels for a dreamlike feel, irregular panels for chaos, and silent panels for a pause. | Hinglish: Har panel type ka apna kaam hota hai: stable aur aasaan reading ke liye standard rectangles, towering cheezon ko dikhane, girne ya pace dheema karne ke liye tall vertical panels, landscapes aur sukoon ke liye wide panels, emotion ke liye close-ups, context ke liye establishing shots, climaxes ke liye splash panels, chhoti details ke liye inset panels, dreamlike feel ke liye borderless panels, chaos ke liye irregular panels, aur pause ke liye silent panels.

Module 119 — Webtoon & Vertical Scroll Storytelling: English: Treating a webtoon like a comic page and packing several panels into one screen, when only about two should be visible at a time. | Hinglish: Webtoon ko comic page ki tarah treat karke ek screen mein kai panels bhar dena, jabki ek waqt mein sirf lagbhag do panels dikhne chahiye.

Module 119 — Webtoon & Vertical Scroll Storytelling: English: Putting too much dialogue in one panel so the reader stops scrolling and starts reading a wall of text. | Hinglish: Ek panel mein bahut zyada dialogue rakhna, jisse reader scroll karna rok deta hai aur text ki deewar padhne lagta hai.

Module 119 — Webtoon & Vertical Scroll Storytelling: English: Spacing every panel the same distance apart so the scroll has no rhythm and time changes are not signaled. | Hinglish: Har panel ke beech ek jaisi distance rakhna, jisse scroll mein rhythm nahi banti aur time changes ka signal nahi milta.

Module 119 — Webtoon & Vertical Scroll Storytelling: English: Using text that looks fine on a monitor but is too small to read comfortably on a phone. | Hinglish: Aisa text use karna jo monitor par theek dikhe, lekin phone par aaram se padhne ke liye bahut chhota ho.

Module 119 — Webtoon & Vertical Scroll Storytelling: English: Skipping silent panels and whitespace, which are the main tools for a dramatic pause in a scrolling format. | Hinglish: Silent panels aur whitespace ko skip karna, jabki scrolling format mein dramatic pause ke liye ye sabse zaroori tools hain.

Module 119 — Webtoon & Vertical Scroll Storytelling: English: Preview every episode on an actual phone before you finalize it, since that is where most readers will see it. | Hinglish: Har episode finalize karne se pehle use asli phone par preview karein, kyunki zyadaatar readers use wahin dekhenge.

Module 119 — Webtoon & Vertical Scroll Storytelling: English: Use whitespace as a pause: a larger gap before a reveal makes the reader scroll through a beat of anticipation. | Hinglish: Whitespace ko pause ki tarah use karein: reveal se pehle bada gap dene se reader anticipation ke ek beat ke dauraan scroll karta hai.

Module 119 — Webtoon & Vertical Scroll Storytelling: English: Vary panel width and shape to mark important scenes, and save a splash or oversized panel for the real climax. | Hinglish: Important scenes ko mark karne ke liye panel ki width aur shape vary karein, aur splash ya oversized panel ko asli climax ke liye bachakar rakhein.

Module 119 — Webtoon & Vertical Scroll Storytelling: English: In Clip Studio Paint, create panels with the frame border tool so the frame masks the artwork and line art cannot spill outside it. | Hinglish: Clip Studio Paint mein frame border tool se panels banayein, taaki frame artwork ko mask kare aur line art uske bahar na nikle.

Module 119 — Webtoon & Vertical Scroll Storytelling: English: I can explain why a webtoon is paced by panel placement and spacing instead of page layout. | Hinglish: Main samjha sakta/sakti hoon ki webtoon ki pacing page layout ke bajay panel placement aur spacing se kaise tay hoti hai.

Module 119 — Webtoon & Vertical Scroll Storytelling: English: I can apply the panel rules of thumb: about two panels per screen, about three dialogues per panel, and generous spacing. | Hinglish: Main panels ke rules of thumb apply kar sakta/sakti hoon: har screen par lagbhag do panels, har panel mein lagbhag teen dialogues, aur bharpoor spacing.

Module 119 — Webtoon & Vertical Scroll Storytelling: English: I can storyboard layout, composition, expressions and dialogue for a vertical episode. | Hinglish: Main vertical episode ke liye layout, composition, expressions aur dialogue ka storyboard bana sakta/sakti hoon.

Module 119 — Webtoon & Vertical Scroll Storytelling: English: I can choose a panel type for a job such as a pause, a climax or a detail. | Hinglish: Main pause, climax ya detail jaise kaamon ke liye sahi panel type chun sakta/sakti hoon.

Module 119 — Webtoon & Vertical Scroll Storytelling: English: Take one four-panel scene from a page comic and re-storyboard it for vertical scroll, leaving at least about 250 px between panels and a much larger gap where time changes. | Hinglish: Page comic ka ek four-panel scene lein aur use vertical scroll ke liye dobara storyboard karein. Panels ke beech kam se kam lagbhag 250 px ki jagah chhodein, aur jahan time change hota hai wahan isse kaafi bada gap rakhein.

Module 119 — Webtoon & Vertical Scroll Storytelling: English: Storyboard ten vertical panels using at least five different panel types from the list, with stick-figure compositions. | Hinglish: List mein diye gaye kam se kam paanch alag panel types use karke stick-figure compositions ke saath das vertical panels ka storyboard banayein.

Module 119 — Webtoon & Vertical Scroll Storytelling: English: Storyboard one short episode with rough sketches, place the dialogue in a clear reading order, then preview it on your phone and fix anything that crowds the screen. | Hinglish: Rough sketches ke saath ek short episode ka storyboard banayein, dialogue ko clear reading order mein rakhein, phir use apne phone par preview karein aur screen par bheed lagne wali har cheez theek karein.

Module 119 — Webtoon & Vertical Scroll Storytelling: English: Draw the same reveal twice, once with a silent panel and a long whitespace pause before it and once without, and write one sentence on how the timing changes. | Hinglish: Ek hi reveal ko do baar draw karein: pehli baar usse pehle silent panel aur lamba whitespace pause rakhein, aur doosri baar inke bina. Phir ek sentence mein likhein ki timing kaise badalti hai.

Module 119 — Webtoon & Vertical Scroll Storytelling: English: What does a webtoon reader see at one time, according to the module? A full page of many panels Two full pages side by side Mostly one panel, which gives a cinematic impression Only text Unlike a page comic, a vertical webtoon shows readers about one panel at a time, which is why placement and spacing control the pacing. | Hinglish: Module ke mutabik, webtoon reader ek waqt mein kya dekhta hai? Kai panels wala poora page Saath-saath do poore pages Aam taur par ek panel, jisse cinematic impression milta hai Sirf text Page comic se alag, vertical webtoon readers ko ek waqt mein lagbhag ek panel dikhata hai. Isi liye panels ki placement aur spacing pacing ko control karti hai.

Module 119 — Webtoon & Vertical Scroll Storytelling: English: How many panels should ideally be visible on the screen at once? At most two At least six Exactly four As many as fit The suggested rule is to present at most two panels on the screen at a time because readers scroll through the strip. | Hinglish: Ek waqt mein screen par ideally kitne panels dikhne chahiye? Zyada se zyada do Kam se kam chhe Bilkul chaar Jitne fit ho sakein Suggested rule hai ki ek waqt mein screen par zyada se zyada do panels dikhayein, kyunki readers strip mein scroll karke aage badhte hain.

Module 119 — Webtoon & Vertical Scroll Storytelling: English: What is whitespace between panels used for? Saving file size Hiding mistakes Making the page look empty As a dramatic pause, and a much larger gap signals a change in time In a scrolling format the gap is part of the timing: about 250 px at minimum between normal panels and roughly 1000 px to signal time passing. | Hinglish: Panels ke beech whitespace ka kya use hai? File size kam karna Mistakes chhupana Page ko khaali dikhana Dramatic pause dena; aur kaafi bada gap time change ka signal deta hai Scrolling format mein gap timing ka hissa hota hai: normal panels ke beech kam se kam lagbhag 250 px aur waqt beetne ka signal dene ke liye kareeb 1000 px rakhein.

Module 119 — Webtoon & Vertical Scroll Storytelling: English: Which panel type is common in webtoons for towering elements, falling, and slowing the pace? Inset panel Vertical (tall) panel Silent panel Borderless panel Tall vertical panels extend downward, show towering subjects or falling, and slow the reading pace for a dramatic effect. | Hinglish: Towering elements, girne aur pace dheema karne ke liye webtoons mein kaunsa panel type aam hai? Inset panel Vertical (tall) panel Silent panel Borderless panel Tall vertical panels neeche ki taraf extend hote hain, towering subjects ya girne ke action ko dikhate hain, aur dramatic effect ke liye reading pace dheema karte hain.

Module 119 — Webtoon & Vertical Scroll Storytelling: English: Why should layouts be designed for mobile screens? Phones cannot show color Because print is not allowed Most webtoon readers use mobile devices instead of computers Because desktop screens are too large Since most readers are on phones, panels, text size and spacing need to be comfortable at that size. | Hinglish: Layouts mobile screens ke liye kyun design karne chahiye? Phones colors nahi dikha sakte Kyunki print ki permission nahi hai Kyunki zyadaatar webtoon readers computers ke bajay mobile devices use karte hain Kyunki desktop screens bahut badi hoti hain Kyunki zyadaatar readers phones par padhte hain, isliye panels, text size aur spacing us screen size par comfortable hone chahiye.

Module 119 — Webtoon & Vertical Scroll Storytelling: English: Easy Paneling Tips for Making a Webtoon O_kids (Okids ART) A free 5-minute video of five paneling points for webtoons, from the creator whose written version is linked below. The video companion to O_kids' written paneling tips, walking through five points for webtoon panels (limit how many panels show on screen, keep dialogue per panel low, vary panel shapes and sizes, set generous spacing, and keep text readable) and ending with a drawing demonstration.

Module 119 — Webtoon & Vertical Scroll Storytelling: English: How to Make a Webtoon: Panel Types for Vertical Scroll Layout, Storyboards, and Thumbnails Walter Ostlie A free 9-minute video on panel types and how to use them in a vertical-scroll storyboard. Walter Ostlie shows the different types of panels and how to use them in vertical-scroll storyboards so a Webtoon reads well.

Module 119 — Webtoon & Vertical Scroll Storytelling: English: How To Pace Your Webtoon: Comicbook Writing Tutorial Walter Ostlie A free 12-minute comic-writing tutorial on pacing a Webtoon. A comic-writing tutorial from Walter Ostlie on how to pace a Webtoon.

Module 119 — Webtoon & Vertical Scroll Storytelling: English: Panelling Tips for Making Webtoon O_kids (CLIP STUDIO TIPS) A free, short article of concrete panel rules for mobile webtoon readers. Explains that webtoon readers see one panel at a time, so pacing comes from panel placement, and gives five points: show at most two panels on screen, keep about three dialogues per panel, vary panel width, shape and size, leave at least 250 px between panels (around 1000 px for a time change), and keep text readable with motion and sound effects. It also shows how Clip Studio's frame border tool masks line art inside each panel.

Module 119 — Webtoon & Vertical Scroll Storytelling: English: [MAKING A WEBTOON] Understanding Storyboard and the Component O_kids (CLIP STUDIO TIPS) A free guide to what a webtoon storyboard should contain, with ten panel types and their functions. Lists the elements a webtoon storyboard should include (panel layout with whitespace as a dramatic pause, character position and composition, expressions and gestures, dialogue and text with a clear reading order, and optional mood notes), then describes ten panel types and what each is for, from standard and tall vertical panels to splash, borderless and silent panels, plus common speech balloon types.

Module 119 — Webtoon & Vertical Scroll Storytelling: English: You can now plan comics for page, manga and vertical-scroll formats. Module 120 steps back to visual development: designing the look of characters, environments and mood before production begins. | Hinglish: Ab aap page, manga aur vertical-scroll formats ke liye comics plan kar sakte hain. Module 114 visual development ki taraf lautkar production shuru hone se pehle characters, environments aur mood ka look design karna sikhata hai.

Module 120 — Visual Development: English: Before a single character is modeled or a single shot is animated, someone has already decided what the whole world should feel like. That decision is visual development. | Hinglish: Ek bhi character model kiye jaane ya ek bhi shot animate kiye jaane se pehle, koi pehle hi tay kar chuka hota hai ki poori duniya ka ehsaas kaisa hona chahiye. Isi ko visual development kehte hain.

Module 120 — Visual Development: English: The worldbuilding arc taught you color scripting, mood, lighting and the concept-art pipeline as separate skills. Visual development is the job where they combine: one artist, or a small team, defining the look of an entire project before production starts. | Hinglish: Worldbuilding arc mein aapne color scripting, mood, lighting aur concept-art pipeline ko alag-alag skills ke roop mein seekha. Visual development woh kaam hai jahan ye sab judte hain: ek artist ya chhoti team, production shuru hone se pehle poore project ka look tay karti hai.

Module 120 — Visual Development: English: It also changes how you build a portfolio. Studios are not only looking for beautiful single images; they want evidence that you can create a unified visual system that other artists can follow. | Hinglish: Isse aapka portfolio banane ka tareeka bhi badal jata hai. Studios sirf khoobsurat single images nahi dekhte; woh yeh saboot bhi chahte hain ki aap ek unified visual system bana sakte hain jise doosre artists follow kar saken.

Module 120 — Visual Development: English: Visual development defines the look, mood and feel of a project in pre-production: the color palette, lighting mood, character style, environment tone and the consistency of the whole world. It is used in animation, games, film and immersive media, and its outputs include color scripts, lighting studies, mood paintings and atmosphere tests, alongside character, costume and environment explorations. | Hinglish: Visual development pre-production mein project ka look, mood aur feel tay karta hai: color palette, lighting mood, character style, environment tone aur poori duniya ki consistency. Iska use animation, games, film aur immersive media mein hota hai. Iske outputs mein color scripts, lighting studies, mood paintings aur atmosphere tests ke saath character, costume aur environment explorations bhi shamil hain.

Module 120 — Visual Development: English: It sits early in the pipeline. Visual development artists work with directors, art directors, production designers and story teams, and their work becomes the visual reference that modelers, animators and lighting artists build from. Some stay on into production so that the finished result keeps matching the original vision. | Hinglish: Yeh pipeline ke shuruati hisson mein aata hai. Visual development artists directors, art directors, production designers aur story teams ke saath kaam karte hain, aur unka kaam visual reference ban jata hai jiske aadhar par modelers, animators aur lighting artists kaam karte hain. Kuch artists production ke dauran bhi jude rehte hain, taaki final result original vision se mel khata rahe.

Module 120 — Visual Development: English: The titles overlap. In practice visual development and concept art are often used almost interchangeably, with feature and TV animation more likely to say visual development and games and live action more likely to say concept art. A useful working distinction is that visual development sets the overall look and consistency (color scripts, lighting style, shape language) while concept art designs specific characters, props and vehicles within it. | Hinglish: In job titles ke beech kaafi overlap hai. Aam taur par visual development aur concept art ko lagbhag ek-doosre ke badle istemal kiya jata hai; feature aur TV animation mein visual development kehna zyada aam hai, jabki games aur live action mein concept art kehna zyada aam hai. Kaam ke liye ek upyogi farq yeh hai ki visual development overall look aur consistency tay karta hai—jaise color scripts, lighting style aur shape language—jabki concept art usi ke andar specific characters, props aur vehicles design karta hai.

Module 120 — Visual Development: English: The work is mostly 2D digital painting, increasingly supported by 3D blockouts for environments and lighting, and it rests on strong fundamentals: drawing, perspective, color, light and storytelling. A strong portfolio shows a unified visual system, with mood explorations, color studies, style variations and the process behind them, and a few strong projects are better than many unrelated pieces. | Hinglish: Yeh kaam zyadaatar 2D digital painting ka hota hai, jisme environments aur lighting ke liye 3D blockouts ka sahara tezi se liya ja raha hai. Iski buniyad strong fundamentals par hoti hai: drawing, perspective, color, light aur storytelling. Ek strong portfolio mein unified visual system dikhna chahiye, jisme mood explorations, color studies, style variations aur unke peeche ka process ho. Kai unrelated pieces ke bajay kuch strong projects behtar hote hain.

Module 120 — Visual Development: English: Treating visual development as one beautiful illustration instead of a system that has to stay consistent across a whole project. | Hinglish: Visual development ko ek khoobsurat illustration samajhna, na ki aisa system jo poore project mein consistent rehna chahiye.

Module 120 — Visual Development: English: Choosing colors and lighting because they look nice rather than because they serve the emotion of the story. | Hinglish: Colors aur lighting isliye chunna kyunki woh achhe lagte hain, na ki isliye kyunki woh story ke emotion ko support karte hain.

Module 120 — Visual Development: English: Filling a portfolio with unrelated pieces instead of a few projects that each show a complete, coherent world. | Hinglish: Portfolio ko unrelated pieces se bhar dena, bajay kuch aise projects ke jo har ek mein ek complete aur coherent world dikhate hon.

Module 120 — Visual Development: English: Showing only polished finals and hiding the explorations, style variations and failed ideas that prove how you think. | Hinglish: Sirf polished final images dikhana aur explorations, style variations aur nakaam ideas chhupa dena, jo yeh dikhate hain ki aap kaise sochte hain.

Module 120 — Visual Development: English: Spreading across every specialty instead of choosing a focus such as character look, environments, color scripting or props and costumes. | Hinglish: Character look, environments, color scripting ya props aur costumes jaise kisi ek focus ko chunne ke bajay har specialty mein haath aazmana.

Module 120 — Visual Development: English: Write the emotional beats of the story first, then let color and lighting follow them, the way a color script does. | Hinglish: Pehle story ke emotional beats likhein, phir colors aur lighting ko unke hisaab se dhalne dein—bilkul color script ki tarah.

Module 120 — Visual Development: English: Build a small world bible for every portfolio project: a palette, a few lighting moods, a shape language, a handful of character silhouettes and key environments. | Hinglish: Har portfolio project ke liye ek chhoti world bible banayein: ek palette, kuch lighting moods, ek shape language, kuch character silhouettes aur key environments.

Module 120 — Visual Development: English: Pick one specialization to be known for, and use the others to support it. | Hinglish: Ek specialization chunein jiske liye aap pehchane ja sakein, aur baaki specializations ko uska support banayein.

Module 120 — Visual Development: English: Keep the explorations. Mood studies, color studies and style variations are the evidence that you can develop a look, not just render one. | Hinglish: Explorations sambhal kar rakhein. Mood studies, color studies aur style variations is baat ka saboot hain ki aap ek look develop kar sakte hain, sirf use render nahi.

Module 120 — Visual Development: English: I can explain what visual development defines and where it sits in the pipeline. | Hinglish: Main samjha sakta/sakti hoon ki visual development kya tay karta hai aur pipeline mein kahan aata hai.

Module 120 — Visual Development: English: I can describe how visual development and concept art overlap and differ. | Hinglish: Main bata sakta/sakti hoon ki visual development aur concept art mein kya overlap hai aur kya farq hai.

Module 120 — Visual Development: English: I can build a small world bible with a palette, lighting moods, shape language and key designs. | Hinglish: Main palette, lighting moods, shape language aur key designs ke saath ek chhoti world bible bana sakta/sakti hoon.

Module 120 — Visual Development: English: I can plan a portfolio project that shows a unified visual system with its process. | Hinglish: Main aisa portfolio project plan kar sakta/sakti hoon jo process ke saath ek unified visual system dikhaye.

Module 120 — Visual Development: English: Take a short story you know and write down the emotional beat of five key scenes in one sentence each. | Hinglish: Apni jaani-pehchani koi chhoti story lein aur uske paanch key scenes ke emotional beats ko har scene ke liye ek sentence mein likhein.

Module 120 — Visual Development: English: Paint three 30-minute mood studies of the same location in three different emotional tones, changing only color and lighting. | Hinglish: Ek hi location ke teen 30-minute mood studies paint karein, har ek ko alag emotional tone dein aur sirf color aur lighting badlein.

Module 120 — Visual Development: English: Build a one-page style guide for an original world: palette, lighting moods, shape language, three character silhouettes and two environment keys. | Hinglish: Ek original world ke liye ek-page style guide banayein: palette, lighting moods, shape language, teen character silhouettes aur do environment keys.

Module 120 — Visual Development: English: Create a six-frame color script for your style guide and ask someone to guess the emotional arc of the story from the colors alone. | Hinglish: Apni style guide ke liye six-frame color script banayein aur kisi se sirf colors ke aadhar par story ka emotional arc guess karne ko kahein.

Module 120 — Visual Development: English: What does visual development define for a project? Only the marketing posters The final animation timing The look, mood and feel of the project, such as palette, lighting mood, character style and environment tone, before full production The business budget Visual development sets the overall visual direction in pre-production so that the whole production can follow one coherent look. | Hinglish: Visual development kisi project ke liye kya tay karta hai? Sirf marketing posters Final animation timing Full production se pehle project ka look, mood aur feel—jaise palette, lighting mood, character style aur environment tone Business budget Visual development pre-production mein overall visual direction tay karta hai, taaki poori production ek coherent look follow kar sake.

Module 120 — Visual Development: English: When in the pipeline does visual development mostly happen? Pre-production, before modeling, animation and lighting begin Only after the film is released Only during post-production After final rendering It is mainly a pre-production role, though some artists stay into production to keep the result consistent with the original vision. | Hinglish: Pipeline mein visual development zyadaatar kab hota hai? Pre-production mein, modeling, animation aur lighting shuru hone se pehle Sirf film release hone ke baad Sirf post-production ke dauran Final rendering ke baad Yeh zyadaatar pre-production ka role hai, halanki kuch artists production ke dauran bhi jude rehte hain, taaki result original vision ke saath consistent rahe.

Module 120 — Visual Development: English: How do visual development and concept art relate? They are unrelated and never overlap Concept art is always 3D and visual development is always 2D Visual development is only for advertising The titles overlap, but visual development sets the overall look while concept art designs specific characters, props and vehicles within it In practice the titles are often used interchangeably, but a useful distinction is overall look and consistency versus specific designs. | Hinglish: Visual development aur concept art ka aapas mein kya rishta hai? Dono ka koi sambandh nahi aur inmein kabhi overlap nahi hota Concept art hamesha 3D hota hai aur visual development hamesha 2D Visual development sirf advertising ke liye hota hai Dono titles overlap karte hain, lekin visual development overall look tay karta hai, jabki concept art uske andar specific characters, props aur vehicles design karta hai Aam taur par dono titles ek-doosre ke badle istemal hote hain, lekin ek upyogi farq yeh hai: overall look aur consistency, banam specific designs.

Module 120 — Visual Development: English: What should a visual development portfolio show? A unified visual system with mood explorations, color studies, style variations and process As many unrelated pieces as possible Only final renders with no process Only character portraits Studios want proof that you can build a coherent look, so a few strong projects with their explorations beat many random pieces. | Hinglish: Visual development portfolio mein kya dikhna chahiye? Mood explorations, color studies, style variations aur process ke saath ek unified visual system Jitne ho sake utne unrelated pieces Bina process ke sirf final renders Sirf character portraits Studios yeh saboot chahte hain ki aap ek coherent look bana sakte hain. Isliye explorations ke saath kuch strong projects, kai random pieces se behtar hote hain.

Module 120 — Visual Development: English: Why write the emotional beats of the story before choosing colors? Because colors are decided by the printer So color and lighting serve the story's emotion instead of just looking nice Because it removes the need for a palette To make the file smaller A color script works when each color choice is tied to an emotional beat in the story. | Hinglish: Colors chunne se pehle story ke emotional beats likhna zaroori kyun hai? Kyunki colors printer tay karta hai Taaki color aur lighting sirf achhe dikhne ke bajay story ke emotion ko support karein Kyunki isse palette ki zaroorat nahi rehti File ka size chhota karne ke liye Color script tabhi kaam karta hai jab har color choice story ke kisi emotional beat se judi ho.

Module 120 — Visual Development: English: Inside Sony Pictures Animation - Visual Development Artist Omar Smith Sony Pictures Animation A free 3-minute official studio video about what a visual development artist does day to day. An official Sony Pictures Animation video about visual development artist Omar Smith and his work at the studio.

Module 120 — Visual Development: English: Sony Pictures Animation - Visual Development Portfolio Tips Sony Pictures Animation A free 3-minute official studio video of portfolio tips for aspiring visual development artists. Official portfolio tips for visual development artists from Sony Pictures Animation.

Module 120 — Visual Development: English: WHAT IS VISUAL DEVELOPMENT? HOW TO MAKE A VIS DEV PORTFOLIO Laura Price A free 8-minute video that explains the field and how to build a portfolio for it. Laura Price explains what visual development is and how to make a visual development portfolio.

Module 120 — Visual Development: English: Visual Development Artist Guide for Creators VEDX (Jay Schnoor) A free overview from a creative studio's blog covering the role, where it sits in the pipeline, how it differs from concept art, and portfolio advice. It is a studio blog rather than an industry-body source, so cross-check job-market claims. Defines a visual development artist as the person who sets the look, mood and consistency of a project before production, listing outputs such as color scripts, lighting studies and mood paintings, explaining that the work happens mostly in pre-production alongside directors, art directors and story teams, contrasting it with concept art, and advising a portfolio that shows a unified visual system rather than isolated pretty pieces.

Module 120 — Visual Development: English: You can now define the look of a whole project. Module 121 narrows to specific designs inside that look: concept art specializations such as character, prop and environment design sheets. | Hinglish: Ab aap poore project ka look tay kar sakte hain. Module 115 us look ke andar aane wale specific designs par focus karta hai: concept art specializations, jaise character, prop aur environment design sheets.

m: Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design
t: Module 121 — Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design: English: A concept artist does not just draw a character or a prop. They answer a question: what should this look like so that the writer, the animator, the modeler and the player all understand it at a glance? | Hinglish: Concept artist sirf character ya prop draw nahi karta. Woh ek sawaal ka jawab deta hai: yeh kaisa dikhna chahiye, taaki writer, animator, modeler aur player—sab ise ek nazar mein samajh saken?

m: Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design
t: Module 121 — Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design: English: Visual development (Module 120) sets the look of a whole project. Specializations are the specific designs inside that look, and they are what most concept art jobs actually ask for: this character, this prop, this vehicle, this creature. | Hinglish: Visual development (Module 114) poore project ka look set karta hai. Specializations us look ke andar ke specific designs hote hain, aur concept art ki zyadaatar jobs mein asal mein yahi maange jaate hain: yeh character, yeh prop, yeh vehicle, yeh creature.

m: Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design
t: Module 121 — Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design: English: This module pulls together skills you already have. Thumbnailing (Module 83), the production pipeline (Module 84) and model sheets (Module 117) all feed into one repeatable process for designing a character or a prop that other people can build from. | Hinglish: Yeh module un skills ko ek saath laata hai jo aap pehle se jaante hain. Thumbnailing (Module 87), production pipeline (Module 88) aur model sheets (Module 111)—yeh sab milkar character ya prop design karne ka ek repeatable process banate hain, jise doosre log dekhkar bana sakte hain.

m: Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design
t: Module 121 — Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design: English: Character design is visual communication. You are telling the audience something about a character purely through how they look, using posing, expression, costuming, props, shape language and color, while keeping the design appealing. Appeal is made of several parts, not one trick. | Hinglish: Character design visual communication hai. Aap sirf uske look ke zariye audience ko character ke baare mein kuch batate hain—posing, expression, costuming, props, shape language aur color ka use karke, aur saath hi design ko appealing rakhte hain. Appeal kai cheezon se milkar banti hai, kisi ek trick se nahi.

m: Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design
t: Module 121 — Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design: English: The process starts with a brief and references, then many thumbnails that focus on silhouette. Each design should look very different from the one before so the art director sees a real breadth of ideas, and you narrow down from there. One direction is then refined with costume and material callouts, followed by a turnaround, expression studies, prop breakouts and layered files for handoff. | Hinglish: Process brief aur references se shuru hota hai, phir silhouette par focus karte hue bahut saare thumbnails banaye jaate hain. Har design pichhle design se kaafi alag dikhna chahiye, taaki art director ko ideas ki asli breadth nazar aaye; phir aap unmein se options chhaantte hain. Uske baad ek direction ko costume aur material callouts ke saath refine kiya jaata hai, phir turnaround, expression studies, prop breakouts aur handoff ke liye layered files banayi jaati hain.

m: Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design
t: Module 121 — Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design: English: Function drives silhouette. Ask what the character does in the project, test silhouettes at small sizes and in shadow, keep the image clean instead of adding extra weapons or outfit layers, make every feature functional, and check proportions against what the character has to do, such as sit, climb or hold a two-handed weapon. A useful test is to hand the sheet to someone who has never read the brief and see whether they can describe the character back to you. | Hinglish: Silhouette ko function guide karta hai. Sochiye ki project mein character kya karta hai, silhouettes ko chhote size aur shadow mein test kijiye, extra weapons ya outfit layers jodne ke bajaye image ko clean rakhiye, har feature ko functional banaiye, aur proportions ko us kaam ke hisaab se check kijiye jo character ko karna hai—jaise baithna, chadhna ya two-handed weapon pakadna. Ek kaam ka test hai: sheet aise kisi insaan ko dijiye jisne brief kabhi nahi padha ho, aur dekhiye kya woh aapko character ke baare mein bata sakta hai.

m: Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design
t: Module 121 — Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design: English: Props are world-building. Every environment is full of them and characters carry them constantly, so a prop should say something about the world and the people who use it, not just fill space. Thinking like a game designer about what the object does in the world is part of designing it. | Hinglish: Props world-building ka hissa hain. Har environment mein props bhare hote hain aur characters unhe lagataar carry karte hain, isliye prop ko duniya aur use karne wale logon ke baare mein kuch batana chahiye, sirf jagah bharne ka kaam nahi karna chahiye. Game designer ki tarah sochna—ki duniya mein woh object kya karta hai—use design karne ka ek hissa hai.

m: Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design
t: Module 121 — Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design: English: Jumping to a rendered illustration before exploring many different silhouettes. | Hinglish: Kai alag silhouettes explore karne se pehle hi rendered illustration banana shuru kar dena.

m: Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design
t: Module 121 — Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design: English: Producing a page of thumbnails that are all small variations of the same idea instead of genuinely different directions. | Hinglish: Thumbnails ka aisa page banana jismein sab ek hi idea ke chhote variations hon, bajaye iske ki alag-alag directions explore ki jaayen.

m: Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design
t: Module 121 — Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design: English: Designing a character that needs a written explanation to make sense. | Hinglish: Aisa character design karna jise samajhne ke liye likhit explanation ki zaroorat ho.

m: Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design
t: Module 121 — Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design: English: Adding extra weapons, layers and decoration that must all be modeled but do not serve the character's function. | Hinglish: Extra weapons, layers aur decoration jodna, jin sabko model karna padega, lekin jo character ke function mein koi madad nahi karte.

m: Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design
t: Module 121 — Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design: English: Treating props as filler that could belong to any world instead of designing them to carry story and function. | Hinglish: Props ko aisi filler cheez samajhna jo kisi bhi world mein fit ho sakti ho, bajaye unhe story aur function dikhane ke liye design karne ke.

m: Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design
t: Module 121 — Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design: English: Write a short brief before you draw: the character's function in the project, one paragraph of history, three to five references and one negative reference that says what you do not want. | Hinglish: Draw karne se pehle ek chhota brief likhiye: project mein character ka function, uski history ka ek paragraph, teen se paanch references aur ek negative reference jo bataye ki aap kya nahi chahte.

m: Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design
t: Module 121 — Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design: English: Generate silhouettes quickly and force each one to be different in overall idea, not just in details. | Hinglish: Silhouettes jaldi generate kijiye aur har ek ko overall idea mein alag banaiye, sirf details mein nahi.

m: Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design
t: Module 121 — Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design: English: Test your favorite silhouettes at very small size and as solid black shapes before refining. | Hinglish: Refine karne se pehle apne favorite silhouettes ko bahut chhote size mein aur solid black shapes ke roop mein test kijiye.

m: Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design
t: Module 121 — Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design: English: For props, ask who made this, who uses it, what world it belongs to and how it is held or operated, and let the answers shape the design. | Hinglish: Props ke liye poochhiye: ise kisne banaya, kaun use karta hai, yeh kis world ka hissa hai, aur ise kaise pakda ya operate kiya jaata hai? Jawabon ko design shape dene dijiye.

m: Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design
t: Module 121 — Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design: English: I can write a short design brief with function, history, references and a negative reference. | Hinglish: Main function, history, references aur negative reference ke saath ek chhota design brief likh sakta/sakti hoon.

m: Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design
t: Module 121 — Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design: English: I can generate silhouettes that are genuinely different from each other and test them at small size. | Hinglish: Main aise silhouettes bana sakta/sakti hoon jo ek-doosre se sachmuch alag hon, aur unhe chhote size mein test kar sakta/sakti hoon.

m: Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design
t: Module 121 — Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design: English: I can take one design through refinement, a turnaround, expression studies and prop breakouts. | Hinglish: Main ek design ko refinement, turnaround, expression studies aur prop breakouts tak le ja sakta/sakti hoon.

m: Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design
t: Module 121 — Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design: English: I can design a prop so that it carries function and says something about its world. | Hinglish: Main kisi prop ko is tarah design kar sakta/sakti hoon ki woh function kare aur apni duniya ke baare mein kuch bataye.

m: Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design
t: Module 121 — Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design: English: Fill in a one-page character brief with function, a one-paragraph history, three references and one negative reference. | Hinglish: Function, ek paragraph ki history, teen references aur ek negative reference ke saath ek page ka character brief bhariye.

m: Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design
t: Module 121 — Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design: English: Do 20 quick silhouette thumbnails of a traveling merchant, making each one noticeably different, then pick the three strongest. | Hinglish: Traveling merchant ke 20 quick silhouette thumbnails banaiye. Har ek ko clearly alag rakhiye, phir teen sabse strong options chuniye.

m: Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design
t: Module 121 — Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design: English: Take one silhouette through refinement, a turnaround and three expression studies, plus a breakout sheet of the props your character carries. | Hinglish: Ek silhouette ko refinement, turnaround aur teen expression studies tak le jaiye, aur saath hi un props ki breakout sheet banaiye jo aapka character carry karta hai.

m: Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design
t: Module 121 — Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design: English: Design three props for the same character that each reveal something different about their world, then write a short brief for a new item in a game you know and design it. | Hinglish: Ek hi character ke liye teen props design kijiye, jinmein se har ek uski duniya ke baare mein alag baat bataye. Phir apne jaane-pehchaane game mein kisi naye item ke liye ek chhota brief likhiye aur us item ko design kijiye.

m: Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design
t: Module 121 — Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design: English: What is character design, in the sense this module uses it? Drawing the prettiest possible outfit Copying an existing character A form of visual communication that tells the audience about a character through how they look Choosing the character's voice Character designers use posing, expression, costuming, props, shape language and color to communicate who a character is, while keeping the design appealing. | Hinglish: Is module ke mutabik character design kya hai? Sabse khoobsurat mumkin outfit draw karna Kisi existing character ki copy banana Visual communication ka ek tareeqa, jo character ke look ke zariye audience ko uske baare mein batata hai Character ki voice chunna Character designers posing, expression, costuming, props, shape language aur color ka use karke batate hain ki character kaun hai, aur saath hi design ko appealing rakhte hain.

m: Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design
t: Module 121 — Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design: English: What should you aim for at the thumbnail stage when designing a character? Many designs that look very different from each other, especially in silhouette, to show a breadth of ideas One final rendered image Five versions of the same silhouette with different details As many colors as possible Art directors want to see a wide range of ideas before a direction is chosen, so each thumbnail should be a genuinely different idea. | Hinglish: Character design karte waqt thumbnail stage mein aapko kis cheez ka aim rakhna chahiye? Aise bahut se designs banana jo ek-doosre se kaafi alag hon, khaaskar silhouette mein, taaki ideas ki breadth nazar aaye Ek final rendered image banana Alag details ke saath ek hi silhouette ke paanch versions banana Jitne ho sake utne colors istemal karna Art directors direction chunne se pehle ideas ki ek wide range dekhna chahte hain, isliye har thumbnail ek sachmuch alag idea hona chahiye.

m: Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design
t: Module 121 — Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design: English: What is a useful test of whether a character sheet is working? How colorful it is Whether it has more than ten details Whether it was drawn quickly Whether someone who has never read the brief can describe the character back to you If a design needs a written explanation to make sense, it is not finished; a stranger should be able to read it from the drawing alone. | Hinglish: Yeh jaanchne ka ek kaam ka tareeqa kya hai ki character sheet kaam kar rahi hai ya nahi? Woh kitni colorful hai Kya usmein das se zyada details hain Kya use jaldi draw kiya gaya tha Kya aisa insaan jisne brief kabhi nahi padha, aapko character ke baare mein bata sakta hai Agar design ko samajhne ke liye likhit explanation ki zaroorat ho, toh woh abhi complete nahi hai; koi anjaan insaan sirf drawing dekhkar use samajh sake.

m: Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design
t: Module 121 — Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design: English: Why are props treated as part of world-building? They are always the most detailed part of an image Props are optional decoration Every environment is full of them and characters carry them, so they can say something about the world and its people They replace environment design Props appear everywhere and are handled by characters constantly, which makes them an efficient way to communicate who made and uses things and what world they belong to. | Hinglish: Props ko world-building ka hissa kyun maana jaata hai? Woh hamesha image ka sabse detailed hissa hote hain Props optional decoration hote hain Har environment mein props bhare hote hain aur characters unhe carry karte hain, isliye woh duniya aur uske logon ke baare mein kuch bata sakte hain Woh environment design ki jagah lete hain Props har jagah dikhte hain aur characters unhe lagataar use karte hain. Isliye yeh batane ka ek asardar tareeqa hain ki cheezein kisne banayi aur kaun use karta hai, aur woh kis duniya ka hissa hain.

m: Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design
t: Module 121 — Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design: English: What does a negative reference in a brief do? It shows an image that illustrates what you do not want, which can save rounds of revisions It lists the character's flaws It replaces thumbnails It is the final render A reference that says 'not this' narrows the design space as effectively as positive references and is rarely included. | Hinglish: Brief mein negative reference kya karta hai? Woh aisi image dikhata hai jo batati hai ki aap kya nahi chahte; isse revisions ke kai rounds bach sakte hain Woh character ki kamiyan batata hai Woh thumbnails ki jagah leta hai Woh final render hota hai ‘Yeh nahi’ batane wala reference, positive references ki tarah design ke options ko limit karta hai, lekin ise aksar include nahi kiya jaata.

m: Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design
t: Module 121 — Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design: English: How professional CONCEPT ARTISTS design characters pikat A free 9-minute overview of how character design works and the process professional concept art teams follow. Explains character design as visual communication, covering the tools designers use (posing, expression, costuming, props, shape language and color), what makes a design appealing, and four steps that many professional concept art teams, including at Riot Games, use to design characters.

m: Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design
t: Module 121 — Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design: English: The "Brain Dump" Method for Character Design Dave Greco (Proko) A free 20-minute demonstration of generating many different character ideas and silhouettes quickly. Uses a traveling merchant to practice character thumbnailing, focusing on generating unique silhouettes and rapid ideas, and explains that thumbnails should show an art director a real breadth of ideas, with each design looking very different from the one before.

m: Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design
t: Module 121 — Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design: English: Design Props like PRO Tyler Edlin and Josh Ash A free 19-minute lesson on prop design as a part of world-building. Josh Ash and Tyler Edlin discuss prop design as a vital part of world-building and show how to level up props from boring and mundane to props that say something about the world and the characters, using a personal fishing-company project as the working example.

m: Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design
t: Module 121 — Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design: English: Concept Art Playbook #9 - Prop Options Ctrl+Paint A free 6-minute design exercise on inventing a new object for an existing game. In this Concept Art Playbook episode the brief is to design a new object to fit an existing game, demonstrated with a new item for Mario Kart 8, and it is approached primarily as a written assignment from the game designer's point of view before any drawing.

m: Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design
t: Module 121 — Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design: English: Character Concept: A 'Make it or Break it' in Game Design Innovecs Games A free article from a games outsourcing studio's blog, useful for its brief checklist and silhouette tests. It is a company blog, so treat its schedule and cost claims as rough guidance only. Describes character concept art as turning a written description into a buildable design, lists deliverables such as thumbnails, silhouette passes tested at small sizes, a refined front view with material callouts, a turnaround, a model sheet with expression studies and prop breakouts, and layered files, and gives a brief checklist (the character's function, a short history, references plus one negative reference, where it will be seen, technical limits, and what is decided versus open) along with game-specific tips such as keeping the image clean and making every feature functional.

m: Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design
t: Module 121 — Concept Art Specializations: Character & Prop Design: English: You can now design specific characters and props inside a project's look. Module 122 moves to how those designs actually get built for games: the game art pipeline from concept to engine. | Hinglish: Ab aap kisi project ke look ke andar specific characters aur props design kar sakte hain. Module 116 mein hum dekhenge ki games ke liye in designs ko asal mein kaise banaya jaata hai: concept se engine tak ka game art pipeline.

Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: A character that looks perfect in a sculpting program can still be unusable in a game, because a game has to draw it many times a second on hardware with a fixed budget. | Hinglish: Sculpting program mein bilkul perfect dikhne wala character bhi game mein kaam ka nahi ho sakta, kyunki game ko fixed budget wale hardware par use har second kai baar draw karna hota hai.

Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: Module 121 ended with a finished design on a model sheet. This module follows that design into production: how a concept becomes an asset that actually runs inside a game engine, and why a concept artist who understands those limits is far more useful to a team. | Hinglish: Module 115 ek model sheet par finished design ke saath khatam hua tha. Yeh module us design ko production tak follow karta hai: concept kaise aise asset mein badalta hai jo game engine ke andar sach mein run karta hai, aur in limits ko samajhne wala concept artist team ke liye zyada useful kyun hota hai.

Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: Games add constraints that illustration and film concept art rarely face: a performance budget, a target platform and a real-time engine. Knowing what the engine is going to ask of an asset lets you design things that are cheaper to build and survive the trip from sketch to screen. | Hinglish: Games par aisi constraints hoti hain jinka saamna illustration aur film concept art ko aam taur par nahi karna padta: performance budget, target platform aur real-time engine. Engine asset se kya expect karega, yeh jaanne se aap aisi cheezein design kar sakte hain jo banana sasta ho aur sketch se screen tak ka safar tay kar paayen.

Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: A game art pipeline turns a concept into an engine-ready asset. A typical 3D path runs from concept and reference, to blocking and a high-detail sculpt, to a clean low-polygon mesh (retopology), to UV unwrapping, to baking detail into textures and texturing, to rigging and animation for characters, and finally to optimization steps such as LODs and collision before import into the engine. A 2D path is shorter: concept, line work, color, export or sprite sheets, then import. | Hinglish: Game art pipeline ek concept ko engine-ready asset mein badalti hai. Ek typical 3D process concept aur reference se shuru hota hai, phir blocking aur high-detail sculpt, clean low-polygon mesh (retopology), UV unwrapping, textures mein detail bake karna aur texturing, characters ke liye rigging aur animation, aur aakhir mein engine mein import karne se pehle LODs aur collision jaise optimization steps aate hain. 2D process chhota hota hai: concept, line work, color, export ya sprite sheets, phir import.

Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: Constraints decide the design. Unity's documentation states that the number of polygons you should use depends on the visual quality you need and the platform you target: fewer polygons run faster because every vertex, edge and face costs computing resources, while more polygons give more detail and control over shape. Its advice for models includes minimizing polygon count, using as few materials as possible, a single skinned mesh renderer and as few bones as possible, while warning that there is no single answer and that you must balance performance against realism. | Hinglish: Constraints design ko tay karti hain. Unity ki documentation ke mutabik, aapko kitne polygons use karne chahiye, yeh aapko chahiye visual quality aur target platform par depend karta hai: kam polygons se cheezein tez chalti hain, kyunki har vertex, edge aur face computing resources leta hai, jabki zyada polygons shape par zyada detail aur control dete hain. Models ke liye uski salah hai ki polygon count kam rakhein, jitne kam ho sake utne materials use karein, single skinned mesh renderer aur jitni kam ho sake utni bones rakhein. Saath hi, woh yeh bhi kehti hai ki iska koi ek hi jawab nahi hai aur aapko performance aur realism ke beech balance banana hoga.

Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: Level of detail (LOD) is how engines handle distance. Without LODs an object is rendered at the same complexity however small it appears on screen. With LODs the engine swaps in simpler versions, reducing polygons, material complexity or the number of renderers. LOD0 is the most detailed version and higher numbers have progressively less detail, and Unreal notes that it switches by screen size rather than by distance, so a smaller instance changes LOD before a larger one. | Hinglish: Level of detail (LOD) woh tareeka hai jisse engines distance ko handle karte hain. LODs ke bina, koi object screen par chahe kitna bhi chhota dikhe, use hamesha ek hi complexity ke saath render kiya jata hai. LODs ke saath engine simpler versions switch karke use karta hai, jisse polygons, material complexity ya renderers ki sankhya kam hoti hai. LOD0 sabse detailed version hota hai aur uske baad badhte numbers mein detail dheere-dheere kam hoti jati hai. Unreal ke mutabik, yeh distance ke bajay screen size ke hisaab se switch karta hai, isliye chhota instance bade instance se pehle LOD badalta hai.

Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: Technical art connects the two sides. Riot Games describes technical art as being, at its core, about streamlining art creation and implementation, which is why artists who understand engine limits are valuable. Decisions are cheapest early: a change at the sketch or silhouette stage costs far less than the same change after rigging. | Hinglish: Technical art dono sides ko jodta hai. Riot Games ke mutabik, technical art ka core kaam art creation aur implementation ko streamline karna hai; isi wajah se engine limits samajhne wale artists valuable hote hain. Shuruaat mein decisions lena sabse sasta padta hai: sketch ya silhouette stage mein kiya gaya change, rigging ke baad usi change ko karne se kahin kam kharchila hota hai.

Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: Designing or sculpting without asking what the target platform and the performance budget are. | Hinglish: Yeh poochhe bina design ya sculpt karna ki target platform aur performance budget kya hain.

Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: Treating polygon count as a purely artistic choice when it depends on the platform and on everything else competing for rendering resources. | Hinglish: Polygon count ko sirf artistic choice samajhna, jabki yeh platform aur rendering resources ke liye compete kar rahi har cheez par depend karta hai.

Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: Ignoring LODs, so a detailed asset is rendered at full cost even when it is a few pixels tall. | Hinglish: LODs ko nazarandaaz karna, jisse detailed asset ko full cost par render kiya jata hai, chahe woh bas kuch pixels jitna hi kyun na dikhe.

Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: Adding extra details, layers and parts that must all be modeled but never read at the distances the player sees them. | Hinglish: Extra details, layers aur parts jodna jin sabko model karna pade, lekin player jitni doori se unhe dekhta hai, wahan woh kabhi nazar hi na aayein.

Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: Waiting until the engine import to discover that a design breaks the rig, the budget or the silhouette. | Hinglish: Engine mein import karne tak intezar karna aur tab pata chalna ki design rig, budget ya silhouette ke saath kaam nahi karta.

Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: Ask for the budget up front: target platform, polygon and texture limits, and how many of the asset will be on screen at once. | Hinglish: Shuru mein hi budget ke baare mein poochhein: target platform, polygon aur texture limits, aur ek waqt mein asset ka kitna hissa screen par hoga.

Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: Check that your silhouette still reads at the lower LODs, since that is what most players will see most of the time. | Hinglish: Check karein ki lower LODs par bhi aapka silhouette samajh aaye, kyunki zyadatar players use hi zyadatar waqt dekhenge.

Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: Preview assets in the engine early and often instead of judging them only in your modeling or painting software. | Hinglish: Assets ko sirf modeling ya painting software mein judge karne ke bajay engine mein jaldi aur baar-baar preview karein.
