Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: Learn the vocabulary of the engine you target (LOD, materials, bones, collision) so you can discuss limits with technical artists and programmers. | Hinglish: Apne target engine ki vocabulary seekhein (LOD, materials, bones, collision), taaki technical artists aur programmers ke saath limits par baat kar sakein.

Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: I can list the main stages of a game art pipeline from concept to engine import. | Hinglish: Main concept se engine import tak game art pipeline ke main stages ginwa sakta/sakti hoon.

Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: I can explain why polygon count, materials and bones depend on the target platform and budget. | Hinglish: Main samjha/samjha sakti hoon ki polygon count, materials aur bones target platform aur budget par kyun depend karte hain.
Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: I can explain what LODs are and how an engine uses them. | Hinglish: Main samjha/samjha sakti hoon ki LODs kya hote hain aur engine unka use kaise karta hai.

Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: I can name the questions to ask about budget and platform before starting an asset. | Hinglish: Main asset shuru karne se pehle budget aur platform ke baare mein poochhe jaane wale sawal bata sakta/sakti hoon.

Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: Write a pipeline checklist for one asset from your Module 121 designs, listing each stage from concept to engine import and who would own it. | Hinglish: Module 115 ke apne designs mein se ek asset ke liye pipeline checklist likhein, jismein concept se engine import tak har stage aur uska zimmedar vyakti shamil ho.

Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: Sketch a prop at three levels of detail (LOD0, LOD1, LOD2) and check whether the silhouette still reads at the simplest level. | Hinglish: Ek prop ko detail ke teen levels (LOD0, LOD1, LOD2) par sketch karein aur check karein ki sabse simple level par bhi silhouette samajh aata hai ya nahi.

Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: Pick a free engine and read its documentation on LODs and importing assets, then write a half-page summary of what an artist must deliver. | Hinglish: Koi free engine chunein aur LODs aur assets import karne par uski documentation padhein, phir aadhe page ka summary likhein ki artist ko kya deliver karna hota hai.

Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: Take one prop from concept to a simple low-polygon model in free software, import it into an engine, and set up two LOD levels, noting where the budget forced you to change the design. | Hinglish: Kisi free software mein ek prop ko concept se simple low-polygon model tak le jayein, use engine mein import karein, aur do LOD levels set up karein. Note karein ki budget ki wajah se aapko design mein kahan changes karne pade.

Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: What is the main purpose of level of detail (LOD)? To make models look more detailed up close only To reduce the rendering workload by using simpler versions of an object as it becomes smaller on screen To change a model's color To increase the polygon count automatically Without LOD an object is rendered at the same complexity no matter how small it appears, so engines swap in simpler versions as it gets smaller. | Hinglish: Level of detail (LOD) ka main purpose kya hai? Sirf paas se dekhne par models ko zyada detailed dikhana Object screen par chhota hote jaaye, to uske simpler versions use karke rendering ka workload kam karna Model ka color badalna Polygon count apne aap badhana LOD ke bina object ko uske chhota dikhne par bhi ek hi complexity ke saath render kiya jata hai, isliye engine object chhota hone par simpler versions switch karke use karta hai.

Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: According to Unity's documentation, what determines how many polygons you should use? The visual quality you need and the platform you are targeting Only the artist's preference Only the file format Only the number of bones The right number depends on the quality you require and the target platform, and fewer polygons run faster while more give more detail. | Hinglish: Unity ki documentation ke mutabik, aapko kitne polygons use karne chahiye, yeh kis baat se tay hota hai? Aapko chahiye visual quality aur aap jis platform ko target kar rahe hain Sirf artist ki pasand Sirf file format Sirf bones ki sankhya Sahi sankhya aapko chahiye quality aur target platform par depend karti hai. Kam polygons tez chalte hain, jabki zyada polygons se zyada detail milti hai.

Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: How does Unreal Engine decide when to switch from one LOD to another in the how-to? Only by the clock By the camera's color settings By screen size rather than by distance, so a smaller instance changes LOD before a larger one By the artist's name The documentation notes that LOD switching is calculated by screen size, not distance, so two instances of different sizes switch at different distances. | Hinglish: How-to mein Unreal Engine ek LOD se doosre LOD par switch karne ka faisla kaise karta hai? Sirf clock ke hisaab se Camera ki color settings ke hisaab se Distance ke bajay screen size ke hisaab se, isliye chhota instance bade instance se pehle LOD badalta hai Artist ke naam ke hisaab se Documentation ke mutabik, LOD switching ka hisaab distance ke bajay screen size se lagaya jata hai, isliye alag size ke do instances alag distances par switch karte hain.

Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: Which of these is one of the performance tips for models given in the Unity manual? Use as many materials as possible Add extra bones for variety Never use polygons Use as few bones and as few materials as possible The manual advises minimizing polygons, using as few materials as possible and as few bones as possible, while balancing against visual quality. | Hinglish: Unity manual mein diye gaye models ke performance tips mein se kaunsa ek hai? Jitne ho sake utne materials use karein Variety ke liye extra bones add karein Kabhi polygons use na karein Jitni kam ho sake utni bones aur materials use karein Manual salah deta hai ki polygons kam se kam rakhein, jitne kam ho sake utne materials aur bones use karein, aur visual quality ke saath balance banayein.

Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: Why should a concept artist learn about game performance budgets? Because concept art is never changed To avoid drawing So designs can be built efficiently and survive the trip from sketch to the engine, since changes are cheapest early Because budgets decide the story Understanding the limits lets you design things that are practical to model and run, and avoid expensive redesigns after rigging or import. | Hinglish: Concept artist ko game performance budgets ke baare mein kyun seekhna chahiye? Kyunki concept art kabhi change nahi hota Drawing se bachne ke liye Taaki designs ko efficiently banaya ja sake aur woh sketch se engine tak ka safar tay kar sakein, kyunki changes shuru mein sabse saste hote hain Kyunki budgets story tay karte hain Limits ko samajhne se aap aisi cheezein design kar sakte hain jo model aur run karne ke liye practical hon, aur rigging ya import ke baad mehange redesigns se bach sakte hain.

Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: So You Wanna Make Games?? | Episode 5: Technical Art Riot Games A free 13-minute official video on technical art, the role that connects art to the engine. Riot Games' episode on technical art, which describes tech art as having many specializations but, at its core, being about streamlining art creation and implementation.

Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: The Complete AAA VIDEO GAME Character Art Pipeline Jared Chavez A free 17-minute walkthrough of a full character art pipeline for AAA games. Presents a complete AAA video game character art pipeline, using an allosaurus concept as the example.

Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: My Full Game Prop Creation Pipeline rileyb3d A free 9-minute look at one artist's pipeline for making a game prop. Walks through the creator's full pipeline for making a game prop.

Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: Creating models for optimal performance Unity Technologies (Unity Manual) Free official documentation on how model choices affect performance in a real engine. Lists tips for performant models (minimize polygon count, use as few materials as possible, a single skinned mesh renderer, as few bones as possible, and keep forward and inverse kinematics separate), and explains that polygon count depends on the quality you need and your target platform, that fewer polygons run faster while more give more detail, and that you have to balance performance against visual realism.

Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: Introduction to level of detail Unity Technologies (Unity Manual) Free official documentation explaining what LODs are and why engines use them. Explains that level of detail improves performance by reducing the rendering workload, because without it an object is rendered with the same complexity however small it is on screen, and describes how LODs reduce polygons, material complexity or the number of mesh renderers, with LOD0 as the most detailed level and higher indices progressively less detailed.

Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: Creating and Using LODs in Unreal Engine Epic Games (Unreal Engine documentation) Free official how-to showing the artist's side of LODs in a second major engine. A how-to on importing a less detailed version of a mesh so the engine swaps between versions as the player moves closer or farther away, noting that the swap is based on screen size rather than distance and that complex collision can use any imported LOD without switching at runtime.

Module 122 — Game Art Pipeline: English: You now understand how a design travels into a game engine. Module 123 turns to animation pre-production: storyboards, animatics and the planning that happens before a single frame is animated. | Hinglish: Ab aap samajh gaye/gayi hain ki design game engine tak kaise pahunchta hai. Module 117 mein hum animation pre-production par aayenge: storyboards, animatics aur ek bhi frame animate karne se pehle ki jaane wali planning.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: A scene can read beautifully on the page and still fall flat on screen. Animation studios find that out in storyboards and animatics, before anyone animates a single frame. | Hinglish: Koi scene page par bahut achha lag sakta hai, lekin screen par phir bhi feeka pad sakta hai. Animation studios ko yeh baat storyboards aur animatics mein pata chalti hai, jabki abhi kisi ne ek bhi frame animate nahi kiya hota.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: Modules 116 to 125 taught sequential storytelling on pages and in scrolling strips. Animation pre-production applies the same thinking to moving images, and it is where a story's shots, staging, timing and designs get tested cheaply, long before production is expensive. | Hinglish: Modules 110 se 125 mein aapne pages aur scrolling strips par sequential storytelling seekhi. Animation pre-production isi soch ko moving images par apply karta hai, aur yahin story ke shots, staging, timing aur designs ko kam kharch mein test kiya jaata hai—production mehenga hone se kaafi pehle.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: It also introduces a role many artists do not expect. A story artist is hired for drawing, but communication and pitching matter just as much, because boards are performed and explained to directors and teams, not just handed over. | Hinglish: Ismein ek aisa role bhi shamil hai jiski kai artists ko ummeed nahi hoti. Story artist ko drawing ke liye hire kiya jaata hai, lekin communication aur pitching bhi utne hi zaroori hote hain, kyunki boards directors aur teams ke saamne perform karke samjhaye jaate hain, sirf unke haath mein thamaaye nahi jaate.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: In a studio pipeline, pre-production starts from a final script and runs several tracks at the same time. The design team breaks down everything the episode needs, starts with rough pre-designs that feed the storyboard artists, then moves to final designs, clean line art, color styling and background paint. The storyboard artists and director do their own breakdown of shots, compositions and action. Casting breaks the script down for voices, runs auditions and records dialogue that is then edited. | Hinglish: Studio pipeline mein pre-production final script se shuru hota hai aur ek hi waqt mein kai tracks par chalta hai. Design team episode ke liye zaroori har cheez ki breakdown karti hai. Woh rough pre-designs se shuru karti hai, jo storyboard artists ko diye jaate hain; phir final designs, clean line art, color styling aur background paint par kaam aage badhta hai. Storyboard artists aur director shots, compositions aur action ki apni breakdown karte hain. Casting team script ko voice roles ke hisaab se break down karti hai, auditions leti hai aur dialogue record karti hai, jise baad mein edit kiya jaata hai.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: Storyboarding is taking scripts, pitches and the early makings of a story and drawing out the shots, the staging and the scenes. The early stage is where a lot of iteration and change happens, because emotional moments that read well on the page may not land on screen and plot problems often appear only once the story has been embodied and stress-tested in boards. | Hinglish: Storyboarding ka matlab hai scripts, pitches aur story ke shuruaati roop ko lekar shots, staging aur scenes draw karna. Shuruaati stage mein bahut saari iteration aur changes hote hain, kyunki page par achhe lagne wale emotional moments screen par asar nahi kar sakte, aur plot ki problems aksar tabhi saamne aati hain jab story ko boards mein dikhakar stress-test kiya jaata hai.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: An animatic is a string of storyboard images edited together with sound to show how a sequence will flow in motion. It adds timing, dialogue, sound effects and music to the same images. It is not always necessary, but it gives a fuller sense of what the finished piece will look and sound like, and even live-action films use animatics for complex action or visual effects scenes. | Hinglish: Animatic, storyboard images ki ek series hoti hai jise sound ke saath edit karke dikhaya jaata hai ki sequence motion mein kaise flow karega. Inhi images ke saath timing, dialogue, sound effects aur music jode jaate hain. Animatic banana hamesha zaroori nahi hota, lekin isse finished piece kaisa dikhega aur sunai dega, iska zyada poora andaaza milta hai. Complex action ya visual effects scenes ke liye live-action films mein bhi animatics use kiye jaate hain.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: The animatic is the review tool. In a studio, board roughs get notes from the director and producers, the cleaned boards go to an animatic editor who cuts them into a timeline, and the team watches it play and breaks it down again. Designs for things that were dropped stop, and designs for things that were added begin, and the animatic keeps being revised with the director and board revisionists until it works. | Hinglish: Animatic review karne ka tool hai. Studio mein, board roughs par director aur producers notes dete hain; phir cleaned boards animatic editor ko diye jaate hain, jo unhe timeline mein cut karta hai. Team animatic ko chalta hua dekhti hai aur phir se uski breakdown karti hai. Jo cheezein hata di gayi hain, unke designs ka kaam ruk jaata hai; jo cheezein jodi gayi hain, unke designs ka kaam shuru hota hai. Animatic ko director aur board revisionists ke saath tab tak revise kiya jaata hai jab tak woh kaam na kare.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: Treating storyboards as finished illustrations instead of a tool for testing staging, shots and story. | Hinglish: Storyboards ko staging, shots aur story test karne ke tool ke bajay finished illustrations samajhna.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: Skipping the animatic, so pacing and timing problems only show up after animation has started. | Hinglish: Animatic skip karna, jisse pacing aur timing ki problems animation shuru hone ke baad hi saamne aati hain.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: Continuing to polish designs for things that the animatic shows are no longer in the story. | Hinglish: Animatic mein jo cheezein ab story ka hissa nahi dikh rahi hain, unke designs ko polish karte rehna.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: Choosing shots and staging so that acting and action are hard to read, which is a common issue in beginner storyboard portfolios. | Hinglish: Aise shots aur staging chunna jisse acting aur action samajhna mushkil ho. Beginner storyboard portfolios mein yeh ek aam problem hai.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: Handing boards over without being able to explain and pitch them. | Hinglish: Boards ko explain aur pitch kiye bina doosron ko de dena.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: Try the three-panel storytelling assignment first: a very small story told in three panels, which teaches visual storytelling without boarding a full sequence. | Hinglish: Pehle three-panel storytelling assignment try karein: teen panels mein batayi gayi ek bahut chhoti story. Isse poora sequence board kiye bina visual storytelling seekhne mein madad milti hai.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: Let sound help carry the load in an animatic, perform the dialogue yourself for the rough track, and choose original music if you will share the piece. | Hinglish: Animatic mein sound ko kaam ka kuch hissa sambhalne dein, rough track ke liye dialogue khud perform karein, aur agar piece share karne wale hain toh original music chunein.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: Show your animatic cold, to someone who has not seen the boards, and note where they get confused. | Hinglish: Apna animatic kisi aise vyakti ko pehli baar dikhayein jisne boards nahi dekhe hain, aur note karein ki woh kahan confuse hota hai.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: Re-run the script breakdown whenever the boards change, so designs and assets follow the story and not the other way around. | Hinglish: Jab bhi boards badlein, script breakdown phir se karein, taaki designs aur assets story ke mutabik hon, na ki story unke mutabik.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: I can explain the difference between a storyboard and an animatic. | Hinglish: Main storyboard aur animatic ke beech ka fark samjha sakta/sakti hoon.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: I can describe how design, storyboard and casting tracks run from a final script. | Hinglish: Main bata sakta/sakti hoon ki final script se design, storyboard aur casting tracks kaise chalte hain.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: I can build a short animatic with timing and scratch sound. | Hinglish: Main timing aur scratch sound ke saath ek chhota animatic bana sakta/sakti hoon.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: I can test boards on a fresh viewer and fix the first point of confusion. | Hinglish: Main boards ko naye viewer ke saath test karke confusion ki pehli jagah theek kar sakta/sakti hoon.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: Tell a tiny story in three panels (setup, turn, ending) and then pitch it out loud, explaining the shot in each panel. | Hinglish: Teen panels mein ek chhoti si story batayein (setup, turn, ending), phir use zor se pitch karein aur har panel ka shot samjhayein.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: Board a short scene in about twelve panels, drawing the same moment with two different staging choices and comparing how clearly each reads. | Hinglish: Lagbhag 12 panels mein ek chhota scene board karein. Ek hi moment ko staging ke do alag choices ke saath draw karein aur compare karein ki dono mein se kaunsa zyada clearly samajh aata hai.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: Edit your boards into a timed animatic with scratch dialogue and simple sound in whatever video editor you have, then watch it back and adjust the timing. | Hinglish: Apne boards ko kisi bhi video editor mein scratch dialogue aur simple sound ke saath timed animatic mein edit karein. Phir use dekhkar timing adjust karein.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: Show the animatic to someone who has not seen the boards, ask them to retell the scene, and fix the first place where their retelling goes wrong. | Hinglish: Animatic kisi aise vyakti ko dikhayein jisne boards nahi dekhe hain, aur usse scene apne shabdon mein dobara sunane ko kahein. Us jagah ko theek karein jahan uski retelling pehli baar galat hoti hai.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: What is an animatic? A finished animated film A character model sheet A string of storyboard images edited together with sound to show how a sequence flows in motion A background painting An animatic turns the storyboard into a timed video with dialogue, sound effects and music, so pacing can be judged before animation. | Hinglish: Animatic kya hota hai? Ek finished animated film Character model sheet Storyboard images ki ek series, jise sound ke saath edit karke dikhaya jaata hai ki sequence motion mein kaise flow karta hai Background painting Animatic storyboard ko dialogue, sound effects aur music ke saath timed video mein badalta hai, taaki animation se pehle pacing ko judge kiya ja sake.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: In the studio workflow described, what is the starting point and how do the tracks run? A final script, with design, storyboard and casting tracks running at the same time A finished animation, with tracks running one after another A music track, with storyboards last A character model, with the script written afterward Pre-production starts from a final script, and the design team, the storyboard artists and director, and casting and dialogue work in parallel. | Hinglish: Bataye gaye studio workflow mein shuruaat kis cheez se hoti hai aur tracks kaise chalte hain? Final script se; design, storyboard aur casting tracks ek hi waqt mein chalte hain Finished animation se; tracks ek ke baad ek chalte hain Music track se; storyboards sabse aakhir mein bante hain Character model se; script baad mein likhi jaati hai Pre-production final script se shuru hota hai. Design team, storyboard artists aur director, aur casting aur dialogue ka kaam parallel mein chalta hai.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: Which of these is one of the tips for making an animatic? Never add sound Use only stock music Skip timing entirely Give it to viewers cold, meaning to someone who has not seen the boards A fresh viewer shows you where the story or pacing is confusing, because they cannot fill the gaps from memory. | Hinglish: Animatic banane ke liye inmein se kaunsi ek tip hai? Kabhi sound na jodein Sirf stock music use karein Timing ko poori tarah chhod dein Animatic kisi viewer ko pehli baar dikhayein—yaani aise vyakti ko jisne boards nahi dekhe hain Naya viewer aapko dikhata hai ki story ya pacing kahan confusing hai, kyunki woh yaad se chhooti hui baatein poori nahi kar sakta.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: Why is the storyboard stage a place for a lot of iteration? Because boards are never reviewed Because emotional moments and plot problems often only show up once the story has been drawn out and tested Because drawings cannot be changed later Because animators dislike boards A script can read well and still not work on screen, so boards and animatics are where those problems get found and fixed cheaply. | Hinglish: Storyboard stage mein bahut saari iteration kyun hoti hai? Kyunki boards ko kabhi review nahi kiya jaata Kyunki emotional moments aur plot problems aksar tabhi saamne aate hain jab story draw karke test ki jaati hai Kyunki drawings baad mein badli nahi ja sakti Kyunki animators ko boards pasand nahi hote Script padhne mein achhi lag sakti hai, lekin screen par kaam na kare. Isliye boards aur animatics mein in problems ko kam kharch mein dhoondhkar theek kiya jaata hai.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: Besides drawing, which skills does the story artist in the video call equally important? Music composition 3D modeling Communication and pitching Rigging Story artists present and pitch their boards, so explaining and performing the story matters as much as drawing it. | Hinglish: Video mein story artist ke liye drawing ke alawa kaunse skills ko utna hi zaroori bataya gaya hai? Music composition 3D modeling Communication aur pitching Rigging Story artists apne boards present aur pitch karte hain, isliye story ko samjhana aur perform karna, use draw karne jitna hi zaroori hai.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: Animation Pre-Production Explained in UNDER 5 MINUTES! ✍️ Nicktoons A free 6-minute official studio walkthrough of 2D animation pre-production by a senior animation production director. Sandi Smith, Senior Director of Animation Production, breaks down the pipeline starting from a final script: three tracks run at once (design, storyboards with the director, and casting with dialogue recording), board roughs get notes and cleans go to an animatic editor who cuts a timeline, and the team reviews the animatic and adjusts designs, adding or dropping items, until it is right.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: Beginner's Guide To Storyboarding for Animation Alan Winn (Alanhuynhworks) A free 12-minute beginner guide from a working story artist in the animation industry. Story artist Alan Winn explains what storyboarding is (drawing out the shots, staging and scenes from scripts and pitches), how boards differ from animatics (boards edited on a timeline and timed with music and dialogue), why early iteration matters because plot and emotional problems appear once a story is embodied in boards, and gives a three-panel assignment that includes pitching, since communication is as important as drawing.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: Common MISTAKES beginning storyboard artists make for animation Toniko Pantoja A free 12-minute critique of the mistakes that hold back beginner storyboard portfolios. A working storyboard artist shares feedback on common things he sees holding back beginners' portfolios and animatics, touching on shot choices, camera, staging and acting.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: how to make animatics | beginners guide patchy cables A free 7-minute guide to making your first animatic. A beginner-oriented guide to making an animatic for people who have never made one, from a creator with a little over three years of experience making them, covering how to turn storyboard frames into a timed sequence.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: What is an Animatic — How To Bring Your Storyboard to Life StudioBinder A free, clear definition of animatics and how they differ from storyboards. Defines an animatic as a string of storyboard images edited together with sound to show how a sequence will flow in motion, explains how it differs from a storyboard (a visual representation of a sequence that breaks the action into individual panels), and covers why to use animatics, including as a rough draft of a project, for planning VFX in live action, and for collaboration.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: How to Make an Animatic: A Step-by-Step Guide StudioBinder A free set of practical tips for building an animatic from boards. Gives tips for making an animatic: let sound help carry the load, perform your own dialogue, choose original music, and give it to viewers cold, plus a short explanation of keyframes.

Module 123 — Animation Pre-Production: Storyboards & Animatics: English: You can now plan an animated sequence before production starts. Module 130 turns to print production: preparing artwork for printing, from resolution and color to bleed and file setup. | Hinglish: Ab aap production shuru hone se pehle animated sequence plan kar sakte hain.
